ideas.behavior_computation: One pass over the Stage-2 TRAIN split sequences only. For each ordered pair (i, j) appearing with j inside a forward window of 5 positions after i in the same sequence, increment c_ij; drop pairs where either item has fewer than 5 occurrences in train; keep the top 8 successors per item by c_ij and set w_ij = c_ij / sum_j' c_ij'. Cache as CSR arrays (row pointer, column index, weight). Refit never; recompute anchors from this fixed graph and the current encoder snapshot at each epoch boundary.

ideas.coupling_path: successor graph -> top-8 weighted neighbour set of item i -> Frechet/Karcher mean a_i in the ball -> log_{a_i}(p_i) -> codebook argmin at level 1 -> exp_{a_i}(q_1) -> log at the new point -> level 2 and 3 codes. The behaviour signal is the only source of the base point and the base point is the only thing that makes the curved log/exp non-trivial; delete either and the numeric code tuple changes at the first argument of the argmin. There is no second loss, no auxiliary head and no post-hoc correction.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If behavioural adjacency is better captured by "equal geodesic displacement from a shared anchor" than by "equal absolute position", transition-neighbour items will share first-level codes and longer prefixes more often than in the behaviour-off and geometry-off configurations, the generative model will emit valid prefixes longer, and Stage-3 test_recall@10 will exceed 0.065 with the diagnostics moving in the same direction. Observed by: (i) first-level code agreement rate over training transition pairs, (ii) mean shared prefix length over the same pairs, (iii) code-tuple Jaccard against the both-off reference, (iv) Stage-3 test_recall@10.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the quantizer of the RQ-VAE, at every level: the target is mapped with log at the item's anchor, the codebook step is taken with exp at the running reconstruction, the next residual is recomputed with log at the new point, and the reconstruction loss is a squared Poincare distance. It also acts in the per-epoch anchor construction (Karcher mean under d_Poincare).
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball of fixed negative curvature c = 1 with Mobius addition, exponential map exp_x(v) = x (+) (tanh(||v||/2) v / ||v||), logarithmic map log_x(y) = 2 artanh(||(-x)(+)y||) ((-x)(+)y) / ||(-x)(+)y||, and d(x,y) = 2 artanh(||(-x)(+)y||); both maps are used at the anchor, at every intermediate reconstruction, and in the reconstruction loss.
ideas.key_change: Replace the Euclidean residual quantizer of the RQ-VAE by a chart-relative geodesic residual quantizer. Each item's target point p_i is written as log_{a_i}(p_i) at a behaviour-derived anchor a_i, each quantized level moves the reconstruction along a geodesic exp_{p-hat}(q_l), and the next residual is taken at the new point; anchors are refreshed every epoch from a stop-gradient encoder snapshot and the training transition graph.
ideas.leakage_boundary: SID construction reads only Stage-2 training sequences, the training item table and training graph statistics; valid/test interactions are never touched, no validation statistic enters any constant, and the anchor/neighbour cache is built before any Stage-2 step and never updated from validation or test. The only measured constant, s = median ||z_i||, is a training-item median. The Stage-3 protocol is untouched.
ideas.motivation: Content-only SIDs are assigned in one global flat coordinate system, so two items that users actually move between can receive unrelated code prefixes, and the residual chain is a straight Euclidean line that has no reason to follow a behavioural neighbourhood. A generative recommender then wastes prefix capacity on content similarity that does not predict the next item.
ideas.novelty: The behaviour signal is not a loss weight, a graph regulariser, a Sinkhorn marginal or a hierarchy constraint. It selects the BASE POINT (gauge) of the curved coordinate system in which every residual is measured and every codeword is decoded, and the residual chain itself advances by geodesic exp maps. The same code tuple therefore means "this geodesic displacement from my own behavioural anchor", which is a different coupling position from behaviour-weighted assignment, curved hierarchy and transition-residual losses: here behaviour enters through log_a / exp_a, i.e. inside the geometric primitive that produces the code.
ideas.observables: (i) first-level code agreement rate over training transition pairs, expected to rise; (ii) mean shared prefix length over the same pairs, expected to rise; (iii) anchor displacement ||log_0(a_i)|| distribution, expected to be non-degenerate (not piled at 0); (iv) code-usage entropy per level, expected not to collapse; (v) code-tuple Jaccard versus the both-off configuration, expected to be far from 1 (the mechanism really reassigns SIDs); (vi) Stage-3 test_recall@10 as the sole judgement, target > 0.065.

risks: (1) The encoder may collapse all p_i near the origin, making anchors and the origin indistinguishable and degenerating the mechanism into the behaviour-off arm; the EMA plus the 0.5 s clamp does not prevent collapse, only mitigates drift. (2) For long-tail items the successor set is tiny or empty, so their anchors are noisy or zero and their codes behave like the behaviour-off arm. (3) Codebooks shared across heterogeneous tangent frames may mix incomparable directions and hurt more than the anchoring helps. (4) With a geodesic residual the first level already absorbs most of the displacement, so levels 2 and 3 can die, which shortens effective prefixes and can lower recall. (5) A per-epoch anchor refresh creates a moving quantization target that can oscillate.
ideas.safeguards: artanh argument clamped to 1 - 1e-7 and all norms floored at 1e-8; points clamped to radius 1 - 1e-5 before every Mobius operation; r_1 radially clipped to 4 s (s is measured, not tuned); anchors clipped to 0.5 s and EMA-smoothed against per-epoch drift; empty or single-neighbour sets fall back to a_i = 0 or a_i = p_j; Karcher iteration guarded against divergence with a step-norm clip of 1.0 and a finite-value check that falls back to the previous anchor; dead codebooks follow the baseline re-initialisation policy only, with no extra hyperparameter; a NaN/Inf in any map aborts that step's quantizer update and keeps the previous codebooks.
ideas.spec_equations:
inputs: item content embeddings x_i (d = 64), Stage-2 train successor CSR graph (K = 8), curvature c = 1, L = 3, |C_l| = 256, beta = 0.25, anchor EMA 0.8, clamp radius 0.5 s, radial clip R = 4 s, eps = 1e-8.
  1. z_i = Encoder(x_i); s = median_i ||z_i|| at epoch 0 (frozen); p_i = exp_0(s * tanh(z_i / s)).
  2. every epoch start, with p_i detached:
     m_i = p_{argmax_j w_ij}; repeat 2 times: m_i <- exp_{m_i}(sum_j w_ij * log_{m_i}(p_j) / sum_j w_ij);
     u_i <- 0.8 * u_i_prev + 0.2 * log_0(m_i); if ||u_i|| > 0.5 s: u_i <- u_i * 0.5 s / ||u_i||; a_i = exp_0(u_i); a_i = 0 if N(i) empty.
  3. forward for item i: r = log_{a_i}(p_i); if ||r|| > 4 s: r <- r * 4 s / ||r||; p-hat = a_i; codes = [];
     for l = 1..3: k_l = argmin_k ||r - c_{l,k}||^2; codes.append(k_l); p-hat = exp_{p-hat}(c_{l,k_l}); r = log_{p-hat}(p_i).
  4. loss = d(p-hat, p_i)^2 / s^2 + sum_l ||sg(r_l) - c_{l,k_l}||^2 + 0.25 * sum_l ||r_l - sg(c_{l,k_l})||^2 (+ baseline content reconstruction from log_0(p-hat)).
  5. SID(i) = (k_1, k_2, k_3).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: takes x_i, the frozen successor CSR graph, the anchor cache and tangent-frame codebooks; returns the code tuple (k_1..k_3) per item, the reconstruction point p-hat, per-level tangent residuals r_l, and the scalar loss. Anchors are a non-differentiable cached buffer; gradients flow to the encoder and codebooks only.

specification.text: Poincare ball with fixed curvature c = 1 (radius 1). Encoder z_i in R^d, scale s = median over training items of ||z_i|| measured at Stage-2 epoch 0 and frozen, p_i = exp_0(s * tanh(z_i / s)). Training-only directed successor counts c_ij from Stage-2 sequences give top-K (K = 8) neighbours and weights w_ij proportional to c_ij. Anchor a_i = two-step Karcher mean of {p_j : j in N(i)} under d_Poincare, detached, EMA-smoothed, clamped to radius 0.5 s; a_i = 0 if N(i) is empty. Quantization with L = 3 levels and codebooks C_l of 256 vectors in the tangent frame: r_1 = log_{a_i}(p_i); q_l = argmin_{c in C_l} ||r_l - c||^2; p-hat_0 = a_i; p-hat_l = exp_{p-hat_{l-1}}(q_l); r_{l+1} = log_{p-hat_l}(p_i); SID(i) = (k_1, k_2, k_3). Loss = d_Poincare(p-hat_L, p_i)^2 / s^2 + sum_l ||sg(r_l) - q_l||^2 + 0.25 * sum_l ||r_l - sg(q_l)||^2, with the baseline content decoder fed log_0(p-hat_L). Cost: at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 1023 items/step) each step performs about 1023 * 3 * 3 = 9.2k exp/log calls, roughly 2 MFLOP, plus an anchor refresh of 24556 * 8 * 2 * 2 = 0.8M map calls once per epoch (about 0.1-0.2 s), so total wall clock is at most about 1.05x baseline and memory grows by 24556 * d floats for anchors plus the cached sparse successor graph (tens of MB).

ideas.title: RQ-VAE residual quantization performed in per-item Poincare charts whose origin is the hyperbolic Frechet mean of the item's training-only successor neighbourhood

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set H_k = Hbar for all k, so kappa_k = kappa_0 and T is unused; everything else identical.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run described above.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace d_{kappa_k} by Euclidean ||u_i - e_k||, keep the same H_k-driven code statistics; kappa_k is logged but unused.
ideas.behavior_computation: One pass over the training split only: for every adjacent pair (item_t, item_{t+1}) increment T[item_t,item_{t+1}]; keep counts and row-normalise at use time. Each epoch, H_k uses T rows of items whose current hard code is k. No validation or test sequence is read.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions in training sequences, aggregated into a row-normalised successor distribution per item, from which per-code successor-branching entropy is measured.
ideas.cost_estimate: One pass over the sparse training transition table per epoch: <= 24556 rows, ~O(10) stored successors each, < 0.5 s CPU per epoch, < 25 min over 3000 epochs, done once. Per step: same 1024 x 256 distance count plus one arcosh and one exp per logit, about 1.3x the quantizer cost and < 5% total step time.
ideas.coupling_equation: l_ik = -d_{kappa_k}(u_i,e_k)^2 / tau, with kappa_k = kappa_0 * exp(H_k(T) - Hbar(T)), where H_k(T) is the behaviour term and d_{kappa} is the curved term.
ideas.coupling_path: Behaviour counts -> per-code branching entropy H_k -> per-code curvature kappa_k -> hyperbolic distance d_{kappa_k}(u_i,e_k) -> assignment q_i -> reconstructed SID -> new hard assignments -> updated H_k. Removing behaviour makes kappa_k constant; removing curvature makes the distance Euclidean; both change the same logits.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If successor fan-out is heterogeneous and global curvature is a real bottleneck, codes in high-branching regions should acquire flatter effective metrics, per-code successor entropy of the top-1 next token should drop, and Stage 3 test Recall@10 should exceed 0.065 with no ablation arm trained. Observable in the per-code curvature histogram and Stage 3 prefix hit-rate.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE quantizer, in nearest-code distance and soft assignment, during Stage 2 only; it does not act in Stage 3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball exponential and logarithmic maps plus the Poincare distance with trainable-free negative curvature kappa_k < 0 per code, kappa_k in [0.25*k0, 4*k0], k0 derived from encoder scale.
ideas.key_change: Replace d(z_i,e_k) in the RQ-VAE assignment with a code-specific hyperbolic distance d_{kappa_k}(u_i,e_k), where kappa_k is a deterministic, scale-relative function of the branching entropy H_k of code k, refreshed by EMA from training-only transitions. The decoder and reconstruction target are otherwise unchanged.
ideas.leakage_boundary: T is built once from the training split before Stage 2 starts; validation and test sequences never enter T; hard assignments used for H_k come only from Stage 2 training batches; Stage 3 is trained and evaluated after SIDs are frozen. No validation/test interaction can change a SID.
ideas.motivation: Items differ in how predictable their training successors are. Items in a high-fan-out region need coarse cells with fine boundaries, while items on a narrow chain need sharp cells. One global curvature forces the same resolution everywhere, so prefix tokens smear across fan-out regimes and Stage 3 cannot separate "many possible next items" from "one likely next item".
ideas.novelty: The curvature is neither a global constant nor a separate loss. Every codebook vector carries its own negative curvature computed from the measured successor-branching entropy of the training items currently assigned to that code, and that curvature enters the quantizer distance itself. Nothing in the repository ties per-code curvature to measured behaviour.
ideas.observables: Per-code curvature histogram; per-code successor entropy of the first SID token; code-usage entropy; Stage 3 test Recall@10; prefix hit-rate at each prefix length.
risks: Entropy feedback can oscillate or collapse items into a few codes; the clamp and post-epoch-500 freeze are the guards. Per-code curvature makes dissimilarity asymmetric, so nearest-code search is no longer a metric nearest-neighbour problem; acceptable because codes are only compared as candidates. If branching entropy is nearly uniform, kappa_k is nearly constant and the mechanism reduces to baseline: safe failure but no gain.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp ||u|| and ||e|| to (1-1e-5)/sqrt(|k|); clamp the arcosh argument to >= 1+1e-7; compute logits in float64; detach T and hard assignments when forming H_k; clamp kappa_k as stated; freeze kappa after epoch 500; carry the previous H_k for codes with zero assigned items.
ideas.spec_equations: z_i = encoder(x_i); u_i = exp_0^{k0}(z_i); T_ij from training transitions; p_kj = (sum_{i:a_i=k} T_ij + 1) / (sum_j (sum_{i:a_i=k} T_ij + 1)); H_k = -sum_j p_kj log p_kj / log M; Hbar = mean_k H_k; kappa_k = clip(k0 * exp(H_k - Hbar), 0.25*k0, 4*k0); d_k(u,e) = (1/sqrt(|k|)) arcosh(1 + 2|k| ||u-e||^2 / ((1-|k||u|^2)(1-|k||e|^2))); l_ik = -d_{kappa_k}(u_i,e_k)^2 / tau; q_i = softmax(l_i); L = L_RQVAE + L_commit; a_i = argmax_k q_ik at epoch end; H_k <- 0.9 H_k + 0.1 H_k^new.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder outputs z_i (batch 1023/1024), codebook E in the Poincare ball, training transition table T, previous H_k. Outputs: soft assignment q_i over 256 codes, hard SIDs, updated H_k, and the usual reconstruction loss.

specification.text: u_i = exp_0^{k0}(z_i), k0 = -1 / median_i ||z_i||^2 (derived from encoder scale, not tuned). For every code k, p_kj = (sum_{i:a_i=k} T_ij + alpha) / (sum_j' (sum_{i:a_i=k} T_ij' + alpha)), alpha = 1, H_k = -sum_j p_kj log p_kj / log M, Hbar = mean_k H_k. kappa_k = k0 * exp(H_k - Hbar) clamped to [0.25*k0, 4*k0] (documented clamp, no sweep). Assignment logits l_ik = -d_{kappa_k}(u_i,e_k)^2 / tau with tau = median_{i,k} d_{kappa_k}(u_i,e_k)^2 computed once at epoch 0 and frozen. q_i = softmax(l_i). Loss = baseline RQ-VAE reconstruction + commitment; only assignment distances and code usage change. At each epoch end recompute hard a_i, accumulate T_ij from the training transition table restricted to items with a_i = k, and update H_k <- 0.9 H_k + 0.1 H_k^new; initialise H_k at global entropy. Freeze kappa_k after epoch 500 (documented warm-up, no tuning).

ideas.title: Behaviour-branching curvature field on the RQ-VAE codebook metric

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: eta = 0, so s_i = u_i and the chain is a plain hyperbolic residual quantizer; the transition table is still built but unused.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run with the successor shift and the hyperbolic residual chain.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace exp_0, log_0, exp_{e}, log_{e} and d_k by Euclidean counterparts (vector addition and L2 distance), keep eta and t_i identical.
ideas.behavior_computation: For each training item i, collect the multiset of its immediate next items in training sequences, keep the 32 most frequent successors, map each successor through log_0^k, average the differences from log_0^k(u_i), and L2-normalise only if ||t_i|| < 1e-8; all from training split.
ideas.behavior_signal: Mean successor displacement in tangent space, computed from directed item transitions in the training split.
ideas.cost_estimate: One extra exp/log per item per level and one successor-mean precomputation pass over training (~24556 items x <=32 successors) done once. Per step: 3 x 1024 x 256 distances with log/exp maps (~2x baseline quantizer arithmetic) plus two reconstruction terms; roughly 1.5x-2x baseline Stage 2 step time, no extra epochs or passes.
ideas.coupling_equation: s_i = exp_0^k(log_0^k(u_i) + eta * t_i) and c_l = argmin_k d_k(b_i^l, e_k), where t_i (behaviour) is transported by the curved exp map and scored by the curved distance.
ideas.coupling_path: Training transitions -> successor tangent t_i -> shifted base s_i -> level-1 nearest code and residual -> levels 2-3 codes -> reconstructed u_hat -> SID and loss. Removing behaviour sets eta = 0 and s_i = u_i; removing geometry replaces exp/log and d_k by Euclidean addition and distance; both alter the same code chain.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If transitions carry directional information that residuals currently destroy, shifting the base along the successor tangent should make true successor pairs share longer SID prefixes and raise Stage 3 test Recall@10 above 0.065 in the single frozen run. Observable as a rise in mean longest-common-prefix of held-out successor pairs and in Stage 3 recall at prefix lengths 1-3.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE residual quantizer during Stage 2: it defines the level-1 base point and the tangent frame of every later level.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball exp/log maps and distance with fixed negative curvature k = k0 = -1/median_i||z_i||^2, used for the base shift and every residual step.
ideas.key_change: Before level 1, shift the item point along its measured successor direction in the tangent space at the origin: s_i = exp_0^k(log_0^k(u_i) + eta * t_i). Then quantize s_i with a hyperbolic residual quantizer whose level-l base is exp_{e_{c_l}}^k(xi_l) and whose codes are chosen by d_k(base, e_k). The reconstruction target remains the unshifted u_i, but the code chain is chosen to reconstruct s_i.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The successor table and eta scale are computed once from training sequences before Stage 2 and frozen; no validation or test sequence contributes a transition, and no Stage 3 feedback changes them.
ideas.motivation: In residual quantization the second and third tokens encode whatever the first code failed to capture, in a direction unrelated to where users actually go next. When training transitions are directionally predictable, that predictability is spent on arbitrary residual bits instead of on a prefix a generative recommender can use.
ideas.novelty: The residual chain is not reweighted and embeddings are not graph-smoothed. The quantizer's base point is transported along the measured mean successor-displacement tangent before the first code is chosen, and every later residual is taken in the tangent space of the chosen code; curvature controls the transport. This is a curved, behaviour-directed residual, distinct from behaviour-weighted distances or graph-regularised embeddings.
ideas.observables: Mean successor LCP of SIDs; SID prefix entropy per level; reconstruction distance under the unshifted target; Stage 3 test Recall@10.
risks: The successor mean is noisy for tail items and can point uninformatively; the median-based eta keeps the shift at one code spacing but tail items may still be displaced too much. The shifted target can fight the reconstruction term and degrade item fidelity; sharing u_hat limits but does not remove this. Hyperbolic residual chains are numerically fragile near the ball boundary.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp all ball norms to (1-1e-5)/sqrt(|k0|); clamp arcosh argument to >= 1+1e-7; log-domain softmax over codes; cap successor out-degree at 32 and drop zero-count entries; if ||t_i|| = 0 use s_i = u_i; compute eta once and freeze it; float64 for exp/log in the first 100 steps.
ideas.spec_equations: u_i = exp_0^{k0}(z_i); t_i = mean_{j in S_i}(log_0^{k0}(u_j) - log_0^{k0}(u_i)); d_code = median_{k != k'} d_{k0}(e_k,e_k'); eta = d_code / (median_i ||t_i|| + 1e-8); s_i = exp_0^{k0}(log_0^{k0}(u_i) + eta t_i); b_i^1 = s_i; for l = 1..L: c_l = argmin_k d_{k0}(b_i^l,e_k); xi_l = log_{e_{c_l}}^{k0}(b_i^l) - log_{e_{c_l}}^{k0}(e_{c_l}); b_i^{l+1} = exp_{e_{c_l}}^{k0}(xi_l); u_hat_i = exp_0^{k0}(sum_l log_0^{k0}(e_{c_l})); L = d_{k0}(u_i,u_hat_i)^2 + d_{k0}(s_i,u_hat_i)^2 + ||sg[u_i]-u_hat_i||^2.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: z_i batch, codebook E, successor tangent table t_i, eta, L = 3. Outputs: code indices c_1..c_L (the SID), reconstructed u_hat_i, loss.

specification.text: t_i = (1/|S_i|) sum_{j in S_i} (log_0^k(u_j) - log_0^k(u_i)), S_i the training successors of i (out-degree capped at 32, most frequent). eta = d_code / (median_i ||t_i|| + 1e-8), d_code = median_{k != k'} d_k(e_k,e_k') measured at epoch 0; a typical successor shift then equals one code spacing, so eta is derived, not tuned. b_i^1 = s_i; c_1 = argmin_k d_k(b_i^1,e_k); xi_1 = log_{e_{c_1}}^k(b_i^1) - log_{e_{c_1}}^k(e_{c_1}); b_i^2 = exp_{e_{c_1}}^k(xi_1); c_2 = argmin_k d_k(b_i^2,e_k); and so on for L = 3 levels. u_hat_i = exp_0^k(sum_l log_0^k(e_{c_l})). L = d_k(u_i,u_hat_i)^2 + d_k(s_i,u_hat_i)^2 + commitment. The second term is the behaviour term, the first keeps item fidelity; both share u_hat, so behaviour changes the code chain that produces u_hat.

ideas.title: Successor-directed tangent base shift for hyperbolic residual quantization

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Remove L_geo (equivalently empty edge set / weight 0); all other losses identical.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run with training transitions and hyperbolic geodesic alignment.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Keep the same sampled transition pairs and prefix anchors, but compute the anchor, segment and residual with Euclidean operations: line segment between u_i and u_j, Euclidean point-to-segment distance, no exp/log.
ideas.behavior_computation: One pass over the training split counting adjacent pairs (item_t, item_{t+1}); store as a sparse list of (i, j, count). At each step sample up to 2048 entries uniformly from this list.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed training transitions (i -> j) with their counts.
ideas.cost_estimate: 2048 pairs x 12 golden-section evaluations x one Poincare distance each per step, about 24.5k extra distances versus 1024 x 256 = 262k quantizer distances, so ~+10% quantizer work and well under +10% total step time. Transition list precomputed once; sampling O(2048) per step; 72,000 steps total.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_geo = (1/|E_b|) sum_{(i,j)} w_ij * dist_{k0}( exp_0^{k0}(sum_{m<=LCP_ij} log_0^{k0}(e_{c_m(i)})), gamma_{k0}(u_i,u_j) )^2 / d_{k0}(u_i,u_j)^2, where w_ij and LCP_ij are the behaviour terms and gamma, dist and d are the curved terms.
ideas.coupling_path: Training transitions define edge pairs -> shared prefix tokens define anchor g_ij -> hyperbolic geodesic between the two item SIDs and curved point-to-segment distance -> gradient on the codebook -> next epoch's SIDs and prefixes. Removing behaviour removes the edges; removing geometry replaces the geodesic segment and Poincare distance by a Euclidean segment and L2 distance; both change the same scalar residual.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If prefix tokens are intermediate beam states in Stage 3, moving the shared anchor onto the geometric path between successor items should make true successors share prefixes more often and make those prefixes more predictive. Observable as an increase in area under the prefix hit-rate curve and Stage 3 test Recall@10 above 0.065 in the single run.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In the Stage 2 training loss on the codebook and encoder, applied to prefix anchors built from codebook vectors; it shapes the SID prefix geometry that Stage 3 consumes.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare exp/log maps, geodesic segment, and Poincare distance with fixed negative curvature k = k0 = -1/median_i||z_i||^2.
ideas.key_change: Add one term per sampled training transition (i -> j): the squared hyperbolic distance from shared prefix anchor g_ij to the geodesic segment gamma(u_i,u_j), normalised by the pair's squared hyperbolic distance. The anchor is the exp-map of the sum of the shared prefix code logs.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition list is built once from the training split before Stage 2 and frozen. Validation and test sequences are never read, and no validation/test metric selects the term weight, LCP threshold or golden-section count; those are documented defaults fixed before training.
ideas.motivation: A generative recommender emits SID prefixes, so what matters is not only that related items are close but that the shared prefix lies "between" them along a path. Euclidean prefix codes have no betweenness: the shared prefix of two successor items can sit far off the line joining them, making the prefix a poor intermediate state for beam search.
ideas.novelty: Behaviour does not weight the distance and is not a second loss. Each observed training transition selects a geodesic segment between two item SIDs, and the corresponding prefix anchor is pulled onto that segment in the Poincare ball. Curvature and behaviour meet inside one geometric residual, unlike a transition loss plus an unrelated hyperbolic regulariser.
ideas.observables: Mean LCP of true successor pairs; prefix hit-rate curve at lengths 1-3; codebook norm distribution; Stage 3 test Recall@10.
risks: At the start no two items share a prefix, so LCP = 0 for almost all pairs and the term is inert until codes agree; warm-up and a minimum-LCP filter help but may make the term arrive late. The geodesic minimum can be flat when g is already close to the segment, giving weak gradients. Optimising this term can distort item-level reconstruction if weight 1 is too strong relative to the baseline loss.
ideas.safeguards: Skip pairs with LCP = 0 and pairs whose items occupy the same batch position; clamp ball norms to (1-1e-5)/sqrt(|k0|); clamp arcosh argument to >= 1+1e-7; float64 for golden-section distance; detach sampled edge indices; cap at 2048 pairs per step; if all pairs are skipped return zero; warm up the term from epoch 1 (documented) rather than thresholding by a tuned LCP value.
ideas.spec_equations: c(i) = (c_1(i),...,c_L(i)); LCP_ij = max m such that c_{1:m}(i) = c_{1:m}(j); g_ij = exp_0^k0(sum_{m<=LCP_ij} log_0^k0(e_{c_m(i)})); v = log_{u_i}^k0(u_j); gamma(s) = exp_{u_i}^k0(s * v); delta_ij = min_{s in [0,1]} d_k0(g_ij, gamma(s)) via 12 golden-section iterations; L = L_RQVAE + (1/|E_b|) sum_{(i,j) in E_b, LCP_ij >= 1} w_ij * delta_ij^2 / (d_k0(u_i,u_j)^2 + 1e-6).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: current SIDs for the batch, codebook E in the ball, sampled transition list with counts, k0. Outputs: scalar L_geo and gradients w.r.t. the codebook (and encoder through code selection, using the straight-through assignment already in the RQ-VAE).

specification.text: LCP_ij = number of leading SID tokens equal for i and j. g_ij = exp_0^k(sum_{m <= LCP_ij} log_0^k(e_{c_m(i)})); if LCP = 0 the pair is skipped (documented default: no shared prefix to align). gamma(u_i,u_j)(s) = exp_{u_i}^k(s * Pi_{u_i}(log_{u_i}^k(u_j))), s in [0,1]. delta(g,gamma) = min_s d_k(g,gamma(s)) via 12 golden-section steps on [0,1]. L_geo = (1/|E_b|) sum_{(i,j) in E_b} w_ij * delta^2 / (d_k(u_i,u_j)^2 + eps), w_ij = transition count, eps = 1e-6, term weight fixed at 1 (documented default). E_b is a uniform sample of at most 2048 training transitions per step. Total loss = baseline RQ-VAE loss + L_geo. No other change to the quantizer.

ideas.title: Transition-pair geodesic alignment of hyperbolic prefix anchors

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: every community gets B_g = N/K, i.e. uniform shells r_lg = (K-1)/(K+1) per level; geometry and learnable offsets unchanged.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Euclidean branch with anchor radius (B_g/N)^(1/d), arithmetic Frechet mean, Euclidean distance and linear projection onto the shell.
ideas.behavior_computation: Training sessions only: consecutive pairs give C; A = C + C^T with self-loops dropped; L-level Leiden partition; B_g = number of level-L leaves under g weighted by item mass; N = total leaf mass.
ideas.behavior_signal: Hierarchical branching (leaf mass B_g) of the training directed-transition graph.
ideas.cost_estimate: One-off tree construction and Frechet precompute over 24556 items on CPU (minutes, before training). Per step only the O(K L d) = 256*3*64 ~ 5e4 elementwise projection plus the d_c terms already computed for assignment, well under 1% of Stage-2 wall clock, and zero marginal Stage-3 cost.
ideas.coupling_equation: e_{l,k} = exp_{m_{l,k}}(eps_{l,k}) with m_{l,k} = exp_0( (2/sqrt(c)) artanh( sqrt(c) (N - B_g)/(N + B_g) ) * u_hat_{l,k} )
ideas.coupling_path: measured B_g -> r_lg -> hyperbolic radius rho_lg -> anchor position m -> d_c assignment -> code index -> SID.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the ball radius given to a prefix should match how many leaves it must separate, broad behaviour communities will occupy large-radius shells and their token will become predictable from a short history; prefix-conditional accuracy rises and Stage-3 recall@10 clears 0.065.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In the codebook parameterisation and in the per-step geodesic projection of atoms, i.e. at quantization time inside Stage 2.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball with curvature -c (fixed c = 1 unless the shared scalar is enabled), geodesic diameters, exp/log maps, Frechet mean by Karcher iteration.
ideas.key_change: Each atom is an anchor plus a small learnable tangent offset; the anchor is the Frechet-mean direction of its training-interaction community placed at the hyperbolic radius implied by that community's measured leaf mass, and every step atoms are geodesically projected back into their shell.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The tree is built once from the training split before Stage 2 and frozen; no validation or test sequence contributes an edge, and the anchor directions come from the frozen item content features that the encoder already consumes, never from val/test interactions.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE spreads every level's codebook over the same latent volume, so a coarse prefix covering a huge behavioural subtree occupies no more room than a leaf covering three items. The generator then has to memorise which of 256 equally sized prefixes is broad, which is exactly the prefix behaviour predictability Stage 3 struggles with.
ideas.novelty: The behaviour statistic sets the RADIUS of each individual atom inside the curved ball, i.e. the atom positions, not the assignment weight and not a loss. The radius is a closed-form tree-embedding quantity, so nothing is tuned.
ideas.observables: radial distribution of atoms per level, code usage as a function of B_g, prefix predictability, Stage-3 test recall@10.
risks: The community tree may disagree with the content geometry and put anchor directions in the wrong cones; hard shell projection can freeze atoms; the Sarkar radius saturates near 1 for huge subtrees and loses radial resolution exactly where branching is largest.
ideas.safeguards: clip r_lg to [1e-3, 1-1e-3]; keep ||eps|| <= 0.25*(rho_lg - rho_parent); clip the artanh argument; communities with no assigned items fall back to the parent anchor; Karcher iteration capped at 10 with a step-norm clip.
ideas.spec_equations: as above, plus delta = half the gap between adjacent anchors' rho values.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: inputs are training transition counts and frozen item content embeddings; outputs are L codebooks of K atoms in B_c^d and, per forward pass, one code index per level per item.

specification.text: Symmetrise training transition counts A = C + C^T; build an L-level community tree (recursive Leiden / normalised cut) with N level-L leaves; for level-l community g, B_g = measured number of leaf descendants; r_lg = (N - B_g)/(N + B_g); rho_lg = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) r_lg); u_hat = unit direction of the Frechet mean of the frozen item content embeddings in g; m = exp_0(rho_lg u_hat); e = exp_m(eps); forward RQ identical to the baseline except that distances are d_c; after each optimiser step project e along the geodesic diameter onto [rho_lg - delta, rho_lg + delta].

ideas.title: Codebook atoms placed on radial shells whose radius is the measured branching of the training transition tree.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: eta_i = 0 so b_i = p_i, the standard autoencoder target.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Euclidean branch with b_i = p_i + eta_i * mean_j (p_j - p_i) and a Euclidean reconstruction loss.
ideas.behavior_computation: From training sessions only: for each adjacent pair (i,j) add j to S_i; c_i = max_j count(i,j) / |S_i|.
ideas.behavior_signal: Sequential co-consumption, specifically each item's set of immediate successors and the concentration of that successor distribution.
ideas.cost_estimate: Successor table refresh is O(E d) once per epoch (E ~ 1e5 edges, d = 64, ~6e6 flops, amortised to ~2.5e5 flops per step) plus one extra exp/log pair per item, O(B d), against the existing encoder step. Negligible in Stage 2, a few MB of CSR storage, Stage 3 unchanged.
ideas.coupling_equation: b_i = exp_{p_i}( eta_i * (1/|S_i|) sum_{j in S_i} log_{p_i}(sg(p_j)) ), eta_i = c_i/(1+c_i)
ideas.coupling_path: behaviour concentration eta_i -> length of the geodesic displacement from p_i -> target b_i -> reconstruction loss -> encoder and codebook update -> SID.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If SIDs encode behavioural role, items with the same successor set collapse onto one code and the generator's next-prefix prediction becomes easier; observed as fewer distinct codes per successor-set cluster, higher prefix conditional accuracy, and Stage-3 recall@10 above 0.065.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In the reconstruction target of Stage-2 training, and hence in the gradient that shapes both encoder and codebooks.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball with curvature -c, exp/log maps based at the item point p_i, geodesic interpolation along the log direction, and a d_c reconstruction loss.
ideas.key_change: The reconstruction target of item i is a point on the geodesic from its own ball point toward the hyperbolic mean of its training successors, displaced by a fraction fixed by the item's measured transition concentration.
ideas.leakage_boundary: S_i and c_i are computed from training sequences only and frozen; the successor point table is refreshed from forward passes over training items only; no validation or test sequence, label or interaction is ever read.
ideas.motivation: Many items are interchangeable given the same successor distribution; giving each its own code wastes generator capacity on distinctions the behaviour does not make. What the next-item predictor needs is the item's behavioural role, not its identity.
ideas.novelty: The behaviour signal changes the RECONSTRUCTION TARGET inside the curved ball. It is not an extra loss term, not a reweighted assignment and not a codebook prior, so the coupling cannot be removed by dropping a regulariser.
ideas.observables: mean number of items per code, code reuse across items with identical successor sets, prefix conditional accuracy, Stage-3 test recall@10.
risks: Over-smoothing can merge genuinely distinct items and collapse recall; the momentum table can lag and create a moving target early in training; c_i is noisy for rare items and can over-shift them.
ideas.safeguards: eta <= 1/2 by construction; set eta = 0 when |S_i| < 2; fully detach the successor table; clamp ||b_i|| <= (1-1e-3)/sqrt(c); clip the log-map argument; skip the update if the target norm is non-finite.
ideas.spec_equations: as above, plus the baseline commitment term of the RQ-VAE.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: inputs are item i, its successor set S_i, its concentration c_i, the current point p_i and the successor table; outputs are the target b_i and the reconstruction gradient.

specification.text: S_i = immediate next items of i in training sessions; c_i = max_j p(i->j); eta_i = c_i/(1+c_i) in [0,1/2]; b_i = exp_{p_i}( eta_i * (1/|S_i|) sum_{j in S_i} log_{p_i}(sg(p_j)) ); loss = d_c(phat_i, b_i)^2 + commitment; successor points p_j come from a stop-gradient table refreshed once per epoch.

ideas.title: The autoencoder reconstructs a geodesic-shifted successor barycentre instead of the item itself.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: kappa_i forced to kappa0 for all i, i.e. every item lives in the same unit-curvature ball; the curved distance code path still executes. No arm is trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full run described above, one training run, 3000 Stage-2 epochs, frozen Stage-3 protocol, no early stopping.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: kbar distance replaced by the Euclidean ||p(z_i)-p(c_k)||^2 on the same vectors with the same commitment weight; the entropy table is still computed and still logged. No arm is trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only, count consecutive pairs (u -> i) over all training sequences, deduplicate repeated (user, item) transitions so one power user cannot dominate, add-one smooth, normalise to p_ij, compute H_i and h_i, store a 24556-vector of kappa_i once before Stage 2 starts.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transition counts and the resulting per-item successor branch entropy.
ideas.cost_estimate: ~786k Poincare distances per step (batch 1024 x 256 codes x 3 levels) replacing dot products, two arcosh/hyperbolic evaluations on that tensor; estimate +3 to +5 ms per step, i.e. ~4-6 minutes over 72,000 steps on four cards, under 5% of Stage-2 wall clock. One pre-pass over the training pairs (order 10^5-10^6 edges) to build n_ij and h_i, a few seconds and ~1 MB for the per-item curvature table.
ideas.coupling_equation: k*(i) = argmin_k (1/sqrt(kbar_ik)) arcosh(1 + 2 kbar_ik ||p(z_i)-p(c_k)||^2 / ((1-kbar_ik||p(z_i)||^2)(1-kbar_ik||p(c_k)||^2))), with kbar_ik = 2 kappa_i kappa_k/(kappa_i+kappa_k) and kappa_i = 1 + H_i/log(|S_i|+1).
ideas.coupling_path: training pairs -> per-item branch entropy -> kappa_i -> kbar_ik -> nearest-code decision and commitment gradient -> codebook entries -> SID assignment of every item. Removing behaviour collapses kappa_i to 1 and the whole path to unit-curvature RQ; removing geometry collapses the decision to Euclidean nearest neighbour.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If hub items really need more separated coarse prefixes, then with curvature on, high-branch items should spread over more distinct level-1 codes than low-branch items (a measurable occupancy/entropy gap), the Stage-3 generator's first-token entropy on hub contexts should drop, and test Recall@10 should exceed the frozen baseline; for the idea to be worth keeping the occupancy gap and the recall gain must both appear in the single run.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside quantization, at every residual level: the nearest-code rule and the commitment term of the Stage-2 RQ-VAE, which is where codebook gradients and SID assignment are decided.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball distance with per-pair negative curvature kbar_ik in [1,2] plus the curvature-scaled tangent-to-ball map tanh(sqrt(kappa) r)/(sqrt(kappa) r).
ideas.key_change: Each item gets kappa_i from its normalised successor branch entropy; the RQ-VAE assigns and commits with a symmetrised Poincare distance whose curvature is the harmonic mean of the two endpoints' curvatures, so codebook gradients, code occupancy and the final SID all move with the training graph.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition graph is built exclusively from training-split sequences that Stage 2 already consumes; no validation or test interaction, no Stage-3 label and no future-item information enters kappa. SIDs are frozen when Stage 2 ends, so nothing from validation or test can propagate back into the IDs.
ideas.motivation: A content-only RQ-VAE gives every item the same geometric room. Items with many behaviourally distinct successors (broad-appeal hubs) get coarse prefixes that cannot separate those successors, while leaf items waste capacity. In a negatively curved space volume grows exponentially with radius, so the place where the training transition graph branches is exactly where more negative curvature buys separation per bit; where it does not branch, extra curvature only adds distortion.
ideas.novelty: Curvature is neither a global hyperparameter nor a trainable scalar. It is a per-item field computed from the training-only transition graph and injected into the pair distance used for nearest-code search, codebook gradient and hence SID assignment. Existing behaviour-aware quantizers reweight the data term of a Euclidean quantizer; here behaviour changes the metric itself, and the metric changes the codes.
ideas.observables: per-item curvature table; level-1 code occupancy entropy split by high/low branch items; fraction of items whose level-1 code differs from the Euclidean baseline; prefix-to-successor predictability on training prefixes; Stage-3 test_recall@10.
risks: The harmonic-mean pair curvature is not a true metric, so assignment may oscillate between epochs; if branch entropy is dominated by a few very high-degree items the field is nearly constant and the mechanism degenerates; if the Stage-3 generator is insensitive to fine prefix differences the extra separation buys nothing.
ideas.safeguards: clamp all ball norms to 1 - 1e-5 before arcosh; clamp the arcosh argument to at least 1 + 1e-7; fall back to the Euclidean distance for any pair whose clamped distance is non-finite; floor |S_i| at 1 and h_i at 0 so items with no observed successor sit at kappa0; freeze kappa after the pre-pass so it cannot co-adapt with the codebooks; assert that the SID assignment is a pure function of the frozen table and the epoch's codebooks.
ideas.spec_equations: as in SPECIFICATION plus pseudocode: build n_ij, h_i, kappa_i once; per step encode z=E(x); for l in 1..3: pz=ball(z); for all k compute d_kbar; k*=argmin; e=c[l][k*]; r=r-e; acc+=e; L = ||x - D(acc)||^2 + 0.25 * sum_l d_kbar(p(r_l), p(e_l))^2 + straight-through codebook update.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: inputs are the item content embeddings x_i, the frozen kappa table and the codebooks; outputs are the three-level SID per item, the trained codebooks and the standard Stage-2 checkpoints.

specification.text: successor distribution p_ij = n_ij / sum_j n_ij with add-one smoothing on the training pair counts n_ij; branch entropy H_i = -sum_j p_ij log p_ij; h_i = H_i / log(|S_i| + 1) clipped to [0,1]; kappa_i = kappa0 * (1 + h_i) with kappa0 = 1 (unit ball, no free constant, no sweep); pairwise curvature kbar_ik = 2 kappa_i kappa_k / (kappa_i + kappa_k) in [1,2]. Points are tangent vectors mapped by p_kappa(w) = tanh(sqrt(kappa)||w||)/(sqrt(kappa)||w||) * w. Distance d_kappa(u,v) = (1/sqrt(kappa)) arcosh(1 + 2 kappa ||u-v||^2 / ((1 - kappa||u||^2)(1 - kappa||v||^2))). ideas.ablation_behavior_off: the repair still runs but with m_i = z_i (item point instead of successor centroid) and the representative chosen by content distance rather than in-degree; geometry untouched. No arm is trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full run as specified, one training run, frozen Stage-2 and Stage-3 protocols.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: the repair uses the Euclidean distance between an arithmetic successor mean and the code vectors, with the same grouping and the same in-degree representative rule. No arm is trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From training sequences only: in-degree = number of distinct users whose training sequence contains the item; successor sets and counts from adjacent training pairs, deduplicated per (user, item); both built once and frozen.
ideas.behavior_signal: Training in-degree per item plus the successor distribution used for the centroid.
ideas.cost_estimate: One hash-grouping and sort over 24,556 SIDs per epoch, O(N log N) with N = 24556, plus re-assignment of the colliding tail (order 2k-6k items) against at most 256 candidate codes each, i.e. under 1.5M distances per epoch vectorised in one batched kernel, ~1-2 ms per epoch on GPU, 1.4-2.0 s over 3000 epochs, well under 1% of total wall clock; no extra parameters and no extra forward passes.
ideas.coupling_equation: SID(i) = (prefix(i), argmin_{c in K_i} d_P(m_i, c)) for i in G_s \ {r(s)}, with r(s) = argmax_i indeg_train(i) and m_i = FrechetMean({w_j : j in S_i}).
ideas.coupling_path: training pairs -> successor centroid m_i and in-degree -> representative selection -> geodesic nearest-candidate rule -> repaired SID for the ambiguous items. Removing behaviour makes m_i = z_i and the rule an arbitrary content tie-break; removing geometry replaces d_P by the Euclidean distance from an arithmetic centroid.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If unreachable duplicates are a real recall cap, then the on-run should show a rise in the number of distinct SIDs, a rise in the share of decoded SIDs whose item has above-median training in-degree, higher prefix-to-successor predictability on training prefixes, and a Stage-3 test_recall@10 gain; one run has to show the assignment shift and the recall gain together.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In Stage-2 post-processing, on the quantizer's decision rule for the colliding tail of the assignment.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare distance on the unit ball, curvature kappa = -1 fixed, applied from a behaviour centroid to candidate codes.
ideas.key_change: After the epoch's assignment, group items by full SID; the highest training in-degree item keeps the ID, and every other member is re-assigned at the last level (or the second level if the parent prefix has no free code) to the code geodesically closest to its training successor centroid.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Both statistics are functions of the training split only and are frozen before Stage 3; the repair reads the epoch's codebooks and the frozen table, never a validation or test sequence, and never a Stage-3 prediction, so no held-out interaction can move an ID.
ideas.motivation: The quantizer maps many items onto the same three-token SID; the generator can only emit one item per SID, so the rest become effectively unreachable and recall is capped by an arbitrary content tie-break that has nothing to do with what users actually do next. Adding codes or a fourth level changes the vocabulary and the Stage-3 protocol; nothing has to change if the ambiguous tail of the assignment is decided by behaviour instead.
ideas.novelty: The curved operation acts on the decision rule for already-ambiguous items only, not on the encoder, the loss or a global assignment. The behaviour centroid is the reference point, the Poincare distance to the candidate codes is the criterion, and the representative of each collision class is chosen by training in-degree, so the SID the generator already emits stays fixed and only the unreachable duplicates are moved to where their successors say they belong.
ideas.observables: number of distinct full SIDs per epoch; share of the repair set that actually moves; mean in-degree of the emitted items; distribution of decoded SIDs over test-time generation; prefix-to-successor predictability on training prefixes; Stage-3 test_recall@10.
risks: Re-assignment can put an item into a code whose content neighbours are unrelated, so the generator's content prior works against it; the repaired assignment is discontinuous across epochs and may make the codebook usage noisy; if collisions are concentrated in a few huge content clusters the free-code search degenerates to level 2 and the mechanism mostly relabels.
ideas.safeguards: never move the representative so the generator's learned emission target is stable; cap the number of repairs per epoch at a measured value (the size of the collision tail at epoch 1) so a degenerate first epoch cannot rewrite the whole vocabulary; skip an item when all candidate codes are occupied by their own representatives; clamp ball norms to 1 - 1e-5 and artanh arguments to 1 - 1e-7; if a repair produces a non-finite distance, leave the original SID unchanged and count it in the log.
ideas.spec_equations: as above plus pseudocode: after each epoch compute SID(i) for all i; group by SID; for each group sort by indeg_train descending; keep the first; for the rest build m_i by three Frechet iterations; collect free level-3 codes in the parent prefix; assign argmin d_P(m_i, c); log group sizes and moves; write the repaired assignment for the next epoch's use.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: inputs are the epoch's SID assignment, the codebooks, the frozen in-degree and successor tables; outputs are the repaired SID assignment used for the checkpoint and by Stage 3, plus the collision and movement logs.

specification.text: Group G_s = {i : SID(i) = s}. Representative r(s) = argmax_i indeg_train(i). For i in G_s, i != r(s): m_i = Poincare Frechet mean (K = 3) of its successor points w_j, j in S_i; candidate set K_i = codes at level 3 inside the current level-2 prefix with free capacity, else all level-3 codes inside the prefix, else the level-2 codes; z* = argmin_{c in K_i} d_P(m_i, c) with d_P(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2||u-v||^2/((1-||u||^2)(1-||v||^2))) on the unit ball; set SID(i) = (prefix, z*) and update the code's membership. Repair is applied every epoch after the optimizer step, on the assignment only, with the codebooks untouched.

ideas.title: Behaviour-directed geodesic reassignment of colliding semantic IDs so the generator's reachable item set stops depending on arbitrary tie-breaks.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: M_l is replaced by the constant 1 on the same top-8 support, so the hinge is uniform over the same graph support and carries no measured transition mass or direction.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The coupled run specified above, trained once on the frozen budget with no early stopping.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: The Euclidean surrogate: d_L becomes ||x - y||_2, log and exp become the identity, and the cone hinge becomes a radial-order hinge relu( ||e_{l+1,b}|| - ||e_{l,a}|| + m ), keeping the same M_l weights and the same codebook roles.
ideas.behavior_computation: Only from the Stage-2 training sequences. For each ordered item pair (i, j) with j in the next three positions of the same training session, count n_ij. Form PMI_ij = log((n_ij * N) / (n_i * n_j)) using item marginals n_i, n_j from the same split, clip to [-4, 4], and keep max(PMI_ij, 0). Aggregate to level l as M_l[a,b] = sum over i with code_l(i)=a and j with code_(l+1)(j)=b of the clipped PMI, row-normalise, and keep the top 8 successors per row.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed item-transition mass, aggregated onto consecutive-level codebook pairs.
ideas.cost_estimate: At the frozen scale (24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch, 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps) the transition matrix is built in one pass over training transitions before training, under 60 s and about 0.1% of the run. Per step the extra work is about 3 levels x 2048 sampled transition pairs = roughly 6k hinge evaluations plus a 256x256 gather and one additional aggregation pass for the geodesic Fréchet-style centroid update; estimated +3 to +6% step time, and 0.8M floats of memory for three 256x256 matrices. No extra epochs and no extra forward passes.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_cone = sum_{l,a,b} M_l[a,b] * relu( <e_{l+1,b} - e_{l,a}, e_{l+1,b} - e_{l,a}>_L + m ), with x_l = exp_{e_{l,a}}( T_l[ argmin_k || log_{e_{l,a}}(x_{l-1}) - T_l[k] ||^2 ] ).
ideas.coupling_path: Parent code a selects row M_l[a, :] of the transition matrix; that row weights a cone hinge on the centroid pair (e_{l,a}, e_{l+1,b}); those same centroids are the base point and the codeword of the log/exp residual step; the exp map output is the quantised vector whose nearest codeword index becomes the SID prefix. Remove behaviour and the weights stop carrying transition structure; remove curvature and there is no cone, no log/exp and no geodesic distance; in both cases the emitted SID assignment changes.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If transition direction is information the prefix should carry, then forcing frequent successor codes into the future cone of their parent code will lower the cone-violation rate and raise the accuracy with which the level-2 code is predicted from the level-1 code, and the Stage-3 generative model will convert that into test Recall@10 above 0.065 in the single frozen run. If the generative model already recovers order from position and session context, the cone term will be inert and recall will stay at baseline.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the Stage-2 residual quantiser, at every quantisation level and every optimiser step: the log map produces the residual to be quantised, the exp map produces the code vector that becomes the SID, and the cone hinge acts on the same centroids that the log and exp maps use.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Lorentz model with trainable negative curvature kappa = -c^2 (c = exp(rho)), geodesic distance d_L(x,y) = (1/c) arcosh(-c^2 <x,y>_L), geodesic log and exp maps at the parent centroid, and the Lorentz future-cone order.
ideas.key_change: Replace the Euclidean residual quantiser with a Lorentz geodesic residual quantiser (log map at the parent centroid, nearest tangent codebook, exp map back), and add a transition-mass-weighted future-cone hinge on the same per-level centroids at every optimiser step, so codebook geometry is jointly shaped by reconstruction and by measured transition order.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Transition counts, item marginals and M_l are computed once from the Stage-2 training split before RQ-VAE training starts, then frozen. Validation and test sequences are never read, no validation interaction is used to choose the margin, the top-8 cut or the cone weight, and Stage 3 only consumes the already emitted SIDs.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE semantic IDs are built by residual reconstruction error alone, so a level-2 prefix is chosen because it reduces distortion, not because the item actually follows the level-1 item in user behaviour. A generative next-item model then has to rediscover transition direction from a prefix code that has already discarded it, and every extra level of RQ depth adds a distortion-driven split that cuts across real user trajectories.
ideas.novelty: The mechanism is not a behaviour-weighted distance, not a hyperbolic latent inserted before an unchanged Euclidean quantiser, and not a standalone hyperbolic auxiliary loss. It makes the SID codebook a partially ordered object: consecutive-level centroids are put under a Lorentz causal-cone order whose strength is the training-only directed transition mass between the corresponding code pairs, and the same centroids serve as the base and target of the log/exp residual step. ideas.observables: Cone-violation rate over positive-M_l training transition pairs, at initialisation versus end of Stage 2; level-2 prefix predictability from the level-1 code on training transitions; SID assignment churn between epoch 500 and epoch 3000; and Stage-3 test Recall@10 against the 0.065 target.
risks: The cone hinge can fight reconstruction and raise effective rank or collision pressure at level 1; M may be too sparse at level 1 because item pairs spread over 256 codes; log/exp near the hyperboloid boundary can produce large tangent norms and unstable gradients; a strong cone constraint could collapse many successors into one cone and hurt diversity; the frozen single run gives no way to distinguish a real gain from seed noise.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp the arcosh argument to at least 1 + 1e-6; renormalise every centroid onto the hyperboloid after each update; clamp ||u||_L to [1e-4, 20/c]; skip cone terms with M_l below 1e-6; gradient clip 1.0; if a centroid norm exceeds 1e4 in float32, reset it to its parent centroid; keep c = exp(rho) and clamp rho to [-1.5, 1.5] so curvature stays strictly negative; fall back to plain Euclidean RQ for a level if fewer than 16 positive-M pairs exist at that level.

(3) exp_e(u) = cosh(c*||u||_L)*e + sinh(c*||u||_L)*u/(c*||u||_L). (4) For l = 1..3: r_l = log_{e_{l-1}}(x_{l-1}); q_l = argmin_k ||r_l - T_l[k]||^2; x_l = exp_{e_{l-1}}(T_l[q_l]); SID prefix = (q_1, q_2, q_3). (5) Total loss L = L_rec + L_rq + 0.1 * L_cone / mean_positive_M. (6) Margin m = 0.1 * median over sampled training transition pairs of (-<Delta,Delta>_L) computed once at initialisation; the 0.1 scale and the normaliser are documented defaults, not swept.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs are the Stage-2 item representation batch, the frozen per-level transition matrices M_l, the tangent codebooks T_l (256 entries per level), and the curvature parameter rho. Outputs are the quantised Lorentz code vectors x_1..x_3, the integer code indices that form the SID prefix, the reconstruction and RQ losses, and the scalar cone penalty with its gradient on centroids and encoder.

specification.text: Let c = exp(rho), kappa = -c^2, rho initialised to 0 and clamped to [-1.5, 1.5]. Lorentz inner product <x,y>_L = -x0*y0 + x_s . y_s, hyperboloid <x,x>_L = -1/c^2. A point y is in the future cone of x iff <y-x, y-x>_L <= 0 and (y0 - x0) > 0. Build M_l once from the Stage-2 training split. papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. In modern CMOS photosensors, smart-pixel technologies have allowed the realization of basic signal processing tasks at the pixel level, in analog format before analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule. Hence, the backpropagation fails if intermediate gradients are zero for some functions in the computational graph, because it causes the gradients to collapse when multiplying with zero. Vector quantization is one of those challenging functions for machine learning algorithms, since it is a piece-wise constant function and its gradient is zero almost everywhere. A typical solution is to apply the straight through estimator which simply copies the gradients over the vector quantization function in the backpropagation. This study proposes a vector quantization technique called NSVQ, which approximates the vector quantization behavior by substituting a multiplicative noise so that it can be used for machine learning problems. papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. Hyperbolic geometry offers a natural alternative for hierarchical representations, but naive hyperbolic extensions introduce geometric inconsistencies: non-associative hyperbolic addition prevents consistent residual aggregation, while standard straight-through gradient estimation ignores the geometry of the latent space. papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. In modern CMOS photosensors, smart-pixel technologies have allowed the realization of basic signal processing tasks at the pixel level, in analog format before analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
papers.title: Representation Collapsing Problems in Vector Quantization

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule. Hence, the backpropagation fails if intermediate gradients are zero for some functions in the computational graph, because it causes the gradients to collapse when multiplying with zero. Vector quantization is one of those challenging functions for machine learning algorithms, since it is a piece-wise constant function and its gradient is zero almost everywhere. A typical solution is to apply the straight through estimator which simply copies the gradients over the vector quantization function in the backpropagation. Other solutions are based on smooth or stochastic approximation. This study proposes a vector quantization technique called NSVQ, which approximates the vector quantization behavior by substituting a multiplicative noise so that it can be used for machine learning problems.
